Saved. Reflection complete.

What was generalizable: this was a VISUAL chart-counting question (count local maxima across line plots on a page), a distinct category from the numeric table-extraction the skill otherwise covers. My 17 vs gold 18 was a classic off-by-one undercount — almost certainly a missed faint/shallow/edge peak or an entire secondary series.

What I saved:
- New reference file `references/chart-local-maxima-counting.md` in the officeqa-treasury-bulletin skill — procedure (render page with `pdftoppm -r 300`, vision-count peaks across ALL series and SUM, not pdftotext) plus the off-by-one pitfalls (count every line including faint ones, watch endpoints/shoulders, process stacked sub-charts separately, prefer the higher count when readings disagree by one since the error is systematically undercounting).
- A pointer line in SKILL.md's "Reference files" section so future runs route to it.
- A compact memory breadcrumb noting visual maxima questions exist and the render-and-sum approach.

Net lesson for next time: when a question says "how many local maxima/peaks on the line plots," it's a vision task — render high-DPI, count every series, and lean toward the higher count if uncertain.
